text:
[LSIG.1.1] The v1 signal aggregations. Each is callable in any expression
position as `<agg>(cursor)` per [LSER.16.1], and readable through the
companion-slot form per [LSER.6]. The time model and accuracy come from the
series declaration.

| Aggregation | Semantics | Element type | Time model | Returns | Backing | At capacity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `active_fraction` | time-weighted fraction of the window the slot was `true` | `Bool` | `sliding` | `Float` | `SeriesBackendIntervalPulse` | refuse |
| `onset_rate` | rising edges per second | `Bool` | `sliding` | `Float` | `SeriesBackendRingBuffer` | drop |
| `integral` | time-weighted ∫x dt | `Float`, `Int` | `sliding`, `all_time` | `Float` | `SeriesBackendNumericIntegral` | refuse |


**At capacity** is what a declared `capacity` ([LSER.13.14]) does when an
identity's backing is full. `active_fraction` and `integral` hold a step
function over the window: a dropped sample would leave part of the window
unaccounted for and the value silently wrong, so each **refuses**, as a bounds
refusal, and the fact is not asserted. Each has a backing of its own, so no
atom carries both policies. `onset_rate` counts edges in the ring buffer it
shares with the sample-weighted aggregations of [LSER.18.1] and **drops** with
them: the oldest sample goes, and with it at most the edge the buffer started
on.

**`Returns` is the representation, not the dimension.** `integral` changes
dimension, and over a slot that carries a unit [LUNI.9.2] requires the author to
strip it in a `let`. A unit-typed value is an `Int`
or a `Float` carrying a compile-time dimension ([LNUL.4.9]), so this column and
that requirement describe different axes of one value.
